title: Rollback risk scorecard and sparse-diff profiler for cache-triggered quality shifts
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, explainable pipeline that assigns a rollback risk score to a config or model change based on sparse-diff profiles of cache-hit vs cache-miss replays. The goal is to detect and quantify quality shifts that are causally attributable to prefix/KV reuse and surface a human-readable scorecard to SRE/PM for fast rollback decisions. This complements existing hit-conditioned audits by focusing on small-but-high-impact semantic deltas and producing a ranked list of suspect patterns and candidate mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard produced automatically for any candidate rollout (model or config) within the canary window
Top-10 sparse-diff patterns per rollout identified with example input/output pairs and token-level alignment
Signal precision >= 80% and recall >= 65% on our labeled regression dataset (lab dataset v2025-02), verified by manual review
Actions exported to Console: 'Hold rollout', 'Proceed', or 'Auto-rollback (if enabled)' with rationale text
Integration tests added to CI that simulate 10 synthetic regressions and verify score > threshold triggers alert
plan: Spike: implement token-aligned sparse diff algorithm and run on historical canaries (2d)
Dataset: assemble labeled set of 2k canary pairs with human judgement on cache-attributed regressions (3d)
Scoring: design a composite rollback risk formula (semantic delta magnitude, frequency, customer-impact weighting) (2d)
Prototyping: build lightweight service that consumes replay logs and emits scorecard JSON (4d)
Console hook: wire scorecard into rollout UI with an explainable summary and link to examples (2d)
QA: run shadow canaries for one week and collect FP/FN rates, adjust thresholds (7d)
Ship gated release behind feature flag and measure metrics for 30 days
technical_notes: Sparse-diff approach: operate on token-level alignment between hit and miss outputs to extract minimal edit spans with semantic similarity scores rather than full-string diffs
Attribution heuristic: require the same seed prompt and model version; compare warm (cache-hit) and cold (cache-miss) replays while controlling for temperature/random seeds where applicable

Scoring components: semantic_distance (embedding cosine on span), occurrence_frequency across corpus, customer_impact_score (derived from route tags), and regression_confidence (ensemble of classifiers)
Trade-offs: sparse-diff is cheaper than end-to-end semantic equivalence checks but may miss paraphrase-level regressions—mitigate by including an embedding-based fallback on the top-k candidate spans
Latency/Costs: service runs as offline canary consumer; target max processing of 100k replay pairs/day per instance. Plan for batching and efficient embedding cache to control cost
False positive mitigation: require N independent examples or minimum frequency before escalating to auto-rollback path
test_plan: Unit tests for token-aligned diffing logic with corner cases (truncation, padding, beam outputs)
Integration test: feed historical canary logs where an intentional cache-induced hallucination occurred; verify scorecard surfaces the correct span and score
Labeling exercise: 3 reviewers label 200 canary pairs to validate precision/recall targets
Stress test: simulate 2500 simultaneous replays to validate pipeline backpressure handling
E2E: enable feature flag in staging, run a 1-week shadow canary, and compare decisions vs. manual SRE review

2025-02-12: Spike completed — token-aligned diff prototype identifies minimal spans and reduces noise vs naive line diff
2025-02-14: Dataset build started — exporting 2k canary examples from last 6 months, labeling plan approved by PM
2025-02-17: Prototype service skeleton merged to feature branch; embedding fallback added to reduce missed paraphrases
2025-02-20: Internal review with SRE/PMs — request to include customer route weighting and to cap auto-rollback to P0 customers only
2025-02-21: Threshold tuning in progress — observed precision 82% on small heldout set, recall 60%; plan to increase recall via ensemble classifier
risk: Overly aggressive thresholds could cause unnecessary rollbacks for low-impact paraphrases. Under-sensitivity could miss small deterministic drifts that compound over time. Reliance on embeddings introduces dependency on embedding-model stability.
remediation_steps: Constrain auto-rollback to P0 routes and require >=3 independent examples
Add manual approver flow in Console for mid-tier rollouts
Maintain an embedding-model pinning policy for scorecard computations
